items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: when Ham was reorganizing and adding to his band why he asked me to join.

ctx.x: I think I didn't ask you something I wanted to about Ham Crawford. I believe it was Wingy, and I, this has been several months back, uh, since I even read the book. But he mentioned Wenslow, Arizona, Ham being out there.

Um, Ham played all out through the West. And when he was with him for a time, when he was also out there with Doc Ross for a time, we talked about that. But, uh, Ham Crawford, uh, organized little bands and took them everywhere. And somehow he would just end up, he'd come into a town and pick all the best musicians and offer them wonderful, a wonderful future. And sometimes it materialized, sometimes it didn't. But at least he always was able to attract the best of the young musicians, because they're always…
And, uh, did he, did you and Wingy work with him at the same time? No.

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: So, I joined the band, again, without the permission of my folks.

ctx.x: So, on Friday nights, I would go up and play with these little bands. Well, of course, I knew that I was going to play in a band. That's all I was going to say. I just had to do that. And, so, pretty soon, I just, without my father's permission, I just left and joined this little band. And, we went to Terrell, Texas, and played in a cafe. And, then we played nights in Athens and all the little Texas towns around 50 mile radius. And, this was really before I ever got out on the road to play with other territory of…
